LMS z-scores and their inverse

Source: R/ref-zscores.R
wgh_lms_z.Rd

wgh_lms_z() converts a measurement to a z-score with Cole's LMS formula \(z = ((y/M)^L - 1)/(L S)\) (or \(\log(y/M)/S\) when \(L = 0\)). With restricted = TRUE it applies the WHO adjustment beyond plus or minus 3 SD, which the WHO uses for weight-based indicators so that the distance between successive SDs stays constant in the tails. wgh_lms_value() returns the measurement at a given z-score, which is how centile curves are drawn.

Usage

wgh_lms_z(y, L, M, S, restricted = FALSE)

wgh_lms_value(z, L, M, S)

Arguments

y

Measurements.

L, M, S

LMS parameters (vectors recycled to the common length).

restricted

Apply the WHO restricted tail adjustment.

z

Z-scores.

Value

A numeric vector.

Examples

wgh_lms_z(30, L = -1.5, M = 18, S = 0.12)
#> [1] 2.973567
wgh_lms_z(30, L = -1.5, M = 18, S = 0.12, restricted = TRUE)
#> [1] 2.973567
wgh_lms_value(2, L = -1.5, M = 18, S = 0.12)
#> [1] 24.23739

# The 3rd, 50th and 97th centiles of height for 10-year-old girls (WHO)
p <- wgh_reference("hfa", 10, "Female")
wgh_lms_value(qnorm(c(0.03, 0.5, 0.97)), p$L, p$M, p$S)
#> [1] 126.6055 138.6363 150.6671
